human_actions_pending.action: Resume Phase 51 Plan 51-04 on a Docker-capable host.
human_actions_pending.context: The authoritative LIVE-07/LIVE-08 scoped proof and the full-workspace compose regression cannot run without Docker. PREFERRED host: the Mac dev machine with Colima — scripts/compose-verify.sh and its sibling scripts/mailpit-verify.sh were written for exactly that environment and need no cloud. AWS EC2 is the documented fallback; see aws_execution_context.

aws_execution_context.note: Reconnaissance recorded 2026-08-04 so a resuming session need not repeat it. Only relevant if no local Docker host is available. NO AWS resource was created, started, or modified.

profiles_probed.detail: Valid credentials but zero EC2/S3/SSM/ECS/CodeBuild permissions.
InvalidClientTokenId — credentials are stale or revoked.

Can start exactly one stopped c7i.4xlarge (i-0ee09bc935472cf8a, us-east-1d, tagged Project=municipal-ocr, no key pair attached). ec2:RunInstances is DENIED, as are DescribeImages/DescribeKeyPairs/DescribeSecurityGroups and all SSM actions.

aws_execution_context.operator_decision: Do NOT borrow the municipal-ocr instance — it belongs to another project. Launch a clean, dedicated, Project=caprun-tagged throwaway instance using operator-provided credentials that allow ec2:RunInstances. Installing Docker on that proof instance is pre-authorized.
required_iam_actions: ec2:Describe* — regions, availability zones, VPCs, subnets, images, instance types, instances, instance status, volumes, tags, key pairs, security groups
ssm:GetParameter / ssm:GetParameters on arn:aws:ssm:*::parameter/aws/service/* — resolve current official AMI ids instead of hardcoding a stale one
ec2:CreateSecurityGroup, ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress, ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup — port 22 from operator egress IP only
ec2:StartInstances, ec2:StopInstances, ec2:TerminateInstances, ec2:GetConsoleOutput — condition-scoped to ec2:ResourceTag/Project = caprun
aws_execution_context.recommended_shape: c7i.4xlarge (16 vCPU / 32 GiB), 60 GB gp3 root, Ubuntu 24.04, us-east-1. The 60 GB covers target/ (~3.4 GB) plus the rust:1, python:3-slim, and axllent/mailpit images. Estimate 30-60 minutes of instance time for both gates.
aws_execution_context.transfer_note: The repo is 33 MB excluding target/ (target/ is 3.4 GB and must NOT be copied); .git is 10 MB. rsync with --exclude=target is sufficient.
aws_execution_context.network_requirement: The proof needs real outbound HTTPS to api.github.com. scripts/compose-verify.sh deliberately does NOT remap api.github.com (only github-mock.caprun.test), so the ENV-01 live GET must reach real GitHub (T-40-06). Default-VPC egress satisfies this.

execution_caveats.description: With OPENAI_API_KEY unset or empty, the v1.4 and v1.8 composed live tests SKIP rather than fail (see cli/caprun/tests/live_acceptance_v1_4_composed.rs:585). Task 2's full-workspace gate can therefore exit 0 with those LLM-sidecar legs never executing.
execution_caveats.impact: Not a Phase 51 acceptance requirement — 51-04 owns LIVE-07/LIVE-08, not the v1.4/v1.8 legs — but if those legs skip it MUST be recorded honestly as a coverage note in 51-LIVE-EVIDENCE.md. Forward a real OPENAI_API_KEY in the host env to make them execute.
execution_caveats.must_not: Do not describe a run with skipped legs as a full-coverage regression.

decisions.decision: Leave LIVE-07, LIVE-08, validation, evidence, and Phase 51 completion pending until both compose commands actually pass.
decisions.rationale: Phase 51 is an evidence gate; compilation or an incapable-host fallback cannot establish the promised non-hybrid LIVE proof.

decisions.decision: Prefer a local Docker/Colima host over AWS for the 51-04 proof run; use a dedicated Project=caprun EC2 instance only as fallback, never a borrowed instance from another project.
decisions.rationale: compose-verify.sh was written for the Mac+Colima dev machine and needs no cloud. Borrowing municipal-ocr's instance mixes projects, incurs cost, and mutates a machine outside this repo's ownership.
